decision_table.name: Determine_OH_Filing_Requirement
decision_table.description: Determine if corporation must file Ohio Commercial Activity Tax (CAT) return. Checks for physical presence, economic nexus, or Ohio registration.

condition.name: has_physical_presence
condition.comment: Has physical presence in Ohio (bright-line presence)

condition.name: has_economic_nexus
condition.comment: Meets Ohio economic nexus threshold ($500K Ohio receipts)

rule.policy:
Ohio CAT: No tax due (Ohio-sourced receipts below $150,000 exclusion threshold).
Filing may still be required if: - Organized in Ohio (Ohio entity) - Registered to do business in Ohio - Has bright-line presence (office, employees, property)
Even if no tax is due, businesses above certain thresholds must file to claim the exclusion. Businesses below $150K may be exempt from filing.
Reference: OH Rev. Code § 5751.02(C) - Exclusion Amount Reference: Ohio Dept of Taxation CAT Publication CAT 1, Section 5 Reference: Form CAT 12 Instructions

actions.action: // Physical nexus established - CAT calculation required result.oh_qualifies_for_no_cat = false;

rule.policy:
Ohio CAT filing required due to physical presence (bright-line presence).
Bright-line presence includes: - $50,000 or more of property in Ohio - $50,000 or more of payroll in Ohio - $500,000 or more of Ohio-sourced receipts - 25% or more of total property, payroll, or receipts in Ohio
Physical presence also includes: - Office or place of business in Ohio - Employees regularly working in Ohio - Tangible property located in Ohio - Ohio entity (organized under Ohio law) - Registered to do business in Ohio
Reference: OH Rev. Code § 5751.01(I) - Bright-Line Presence Test Reference: OH Rev. Code § 5751.01(D) - Doing Business in Ohio Reference: Ohio Dept of Taxation CAT Publication CAT 1, Section 3

actions.action: // Economic nexus established - CAT calculation required result.oh_qualifies_for_no_cat = false;

rule.policy:
Ohio CAT filing required due to economic nexus.
Economic nexus threshold: $500,000 in Ohio-sourced gross receipts
This is consistent with bright-line presence standards. Businesses meeting economic nexus must register with Ohio and file CAT.
Situsing (sourcing) rules determine which receipts are "Ohio-sourced": - Sale of tangible property: Destination (where shipped/delivered) - Services: Location where benefit is received - Rentals: Location of property - Digital goods: Location of customer
Reference: OH Rev. Code § 5751.01(I) - Bright-Line Presence Reference: OH Rev. Code § 5751.033 - Situsing Receipts Reference: Ohio Dept of Taxation CAT Publication CAT 2 (Situsing)

No Ohio nexus - no CAT filing requirement.
Corporation does not have: - Physical presence in Ohio (bright-line presence) - $500,000 or more in Ohio-sourced receipts
Any estimated CAT payments would be refunded.
Reference: OH Rev. Code § 5751.01 - Nexus and Definitions Reference: Ohio Dept of Taxation CAT Publication CAT 1, Section 3

decision_table.name: Calculate_OH_Taxable_Gross_Receipts
decision_table.description: Calculate Ohio taxable gross receipts for CAT. Applies situsing rules to determine Ohio-sourced receipts.

condition.name: has_nexus
condition.comment: Has nexus and above exclusion threshold

condition.name: has_excluded_receipts
condition.comment: Has receipts excluded from CAT calculation

actions.action: // No nexus or below threshold - no calculation needed result.oh_taxable_gross_receipts = 0.0;

rule.policy: No Ohio CAT due - gross receipts calculation not applicable.

Ohio CAT: Calculating taxable gross receipts with exclusions.
Taxable Gross Receipts Calculation: 1. Total gross receipts from all sources: [Amount] 2. Apply situsing rules to determine Ohio portion: [OH-sourced receipts] 3. Subtract excluded receipts: - [Exclusions] 4. Ohio taxable gross receipts: = [Final amount subject to CAT]
Common Exclusions: - Receipts from sales to federal government - Receipts from qualifying affiliate transactions - Interest income (in some cases) - Dividend income (in some cases) - Previously taxed receipts (anti-pyramiding) - ISO services (internal support to corporate affiliates)
Situsing Rules (OH Rev. Code § 5751.033): - Tangible personal property: Destination state (where delivered) - Services: Where benefit of service is received - Rents/leases: Location of property - Intangible property: Where property is used - Digital goods: Location of customer/user
Reference: OH Rev. Code § 5751.01(F) - Taxable Gross Receipts Reference: OH Rev. Code § 5751.033 - Situsing Receipts Reference: OH Rev. Code § 5751.01(E) - Exclusions Reference: Ohio Dept of Taxation CAT Publication CAT 2 (Situsing)

Ohio CAT: Using Ohio-sourced gross receipts (no exclusions).
Taxable Gross Receipts Calculation: 1. Total gross receipts from all sources: [Amount] 2. Apply situsing rules to determine Ohio portion: [OH-sourced] 3. Ohio taxable gross receipts: = [Amount subject to CAT]
The CAT is based on GROSS receipts, meaning: - NO deduction for cost of goods sold (COGS) - NO deduction for operating expenses - NO deduction for wages/compensation - NO deduction for losses - NO deduction for depreciation or amortization
This is fundamentally different from an income tax. The CAT applies to gross revenue, not net income or profit.
Situsing Rules (OH Rev. Code § 5751.033): - Tangible personal property: Destination state - Services: Where benefit is received - Rents/leases: Location of property
Reference: OH Rev. Code § 5751.01(F) - Taxable Gross Receipts Definition Reference: OH Rev. Code § 5751.033 - Situsing Receipts to Ohio Reference: Ohio Dept of Taxation CAT Publication CAT 1, Section 4

decision_table.name: Calculate_OH_CAT
decision_table.description: Calculate Ohio Commercial Activity Tax (CAT) liability. Applies $150 minimum or 0.26% rate based on gross receipts.

condition.name: has_nexus
condition.comment: Has nexus and above exclusion threshold

condition.name: above_minimum_threshold
condition.comment: Ohio receipts at or above $1M (subject to percentage tax)

rule.policy:
No Ohio Commercial Activity Tax due.
Reasons: - No nexus with Ohio, OR - Ohio-sourced gross receipts below $150,000 exclusion threshold
Any estimated CAT payments will be refunded.
Reference: OH Rev. Code § 5751.02(C) - Exclusion Amount

Ohio Commercial Activity Tax: Percentage rate calculation.
CAT Calculation (receipts over $1 million): 1. Ohio taxable gross receipts: [Amount] 2. Exclusion threshold: - $1,000,000 3. Receipts subject to percentage: = [Amount] 4. CAT rate: × 0.26% (0.0026) 5. Percentage tax: = [Amount] 6. Minimum tax: + $150 7. Total CAT liability: = [Tax]
Example: $5,000,000 in Ohio receipts ($5,000,000 - $1,000,000) × 0.0026 = $10,400 $10,400 + $150 = $10,550 total CAT
IMPORTANT: This is NOT a corporate income tax. Ohio eliminated its corporate income tax in 2014. The CAT is a gross receipts tax.
Key Differences from Income Tax: - Based on gross receipts, not net income or profit - No deductions for any expenses (COGS, wages, rent, etc.) - Much lower rate (0.26% vs typical 5-10% income tax rates) - No loss carryforwards or carrybacks - No tax credits available
The CAT is paid in addition to any federal corporate income tax. Businesses must pay CAT even if operating at a loss.
Filing Requirements: - Annual return (Form CAT 12) due May 10 - Quarterly estimated payments if annual tax exceeds $1,000 - Electronic filing required for most businesses
Reference: OH Rev. Code § 5751.02(A) - CAT Rate Reference: OH Rev. Code § 5751.02(B) - Minimum Tax Reference: OH Rev. Code § 5751.03 - Tax Calculation Reference: Ohio Dept of Taxation Form CAT 12 Instructions

Ohio Commercial Activity Tax: Minimum tax.
CAT Calculation (receipts $150,000 to $999,999): 1. Ohio taxable gross receipts: [Between $150K and $1M] 2. CAT liability: $150 (minimum tax)
The minimum tax applies to all businesses with Ohio-sourced gross receipts between $150,000 and $1,000,000.
Once receipts exceed $1,000,000, the tax is calculated as: $150 minimum + 0.26% on receipts over $1M
IMPORTANT: This is NOT an income tax. The CAT is based on gross receipts regardless of profit or loss.
Key Features: - Flat $150 tax for receipts $150K-$999,999 - No deductions for expenses of any kind - Must be paid even if business operates at a loss - No tax credits available - Simple calculation (no complex brackets or deductions)
The CAT replaced Ohio's corporate franchise tax and corporate income tax in 2005-2010. Ohio fully eliminated its corporate income tax in 2014.
Filing Requirements: - Annual return (Form CAT 12) due May 10 - No quarterly estimated payments required if annual tax is $150 - Electronic filing required for businesses above certain thresholds
Reference: OH Rev. Code § 5751.02(B) - Minimum Tax Reference: OH Rev. Code § 5751.02(C) - Exclusion Amount Reference: Ohio Dept of Taxation CAT Publication CAT 1, Section 7 Reference: Ohio Dept of Taxation Form CAT 12 Instructions

No Ohio Commercial Activity Tax due - no taxable gross receipts.
Possible reasons: - All receipts excluded from CAT - No receipts sitused (sourced) to Ohio - Business has no sales or revenue
Any estimated CAT payments will be refunded.
Note: The CAT has no loss carryforward provisions like income tax. Each year stands alone based on that year's gross receipts.
Reference: OH Rev. Code § 5751.01(F) - Taxable Gross Receipts Reference: OH Rev. Code § 5751.033 - Situsing Receipts
